title: What is the difference between SOA and microservices (ESB vs lightweight protocols, coarse vs fine-grained, shared vs per-service data, centralized vs decentralized governance)?
shortTitle: What is the difference between SOA and microservices
keyPoints: SOA services are coarse-grained and enterprise-scoped; microservices are fine-grained and bounded to a single capability.
SOA routes through a smart central ESB with SOAP; microservices use smart endpoints and dumb pipes (REST, gRPC, Kafka).
SOA services often share a common enterprise database; microservices follow database-per-service.
SOA governance is centralized with canonical data models; microservices embrace decentralized, polyglot governance.
Microservices are independently deployable and independently scalable; SOA services are typically deployed in larger units.
Microservices add real distributed complexity and only pay off with multiple teams needing independence.
Neither is universally better; the right choice depends on organizational context and trade-offs.

s1_definition.oneliner: SOA is coarse-grained services on a central smart ESB sharing data under central governance; microservices are fine-grained, independently deployable services on lightweight protocols, each owning its own data under decentralized governance.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Granularity** – SOA services are coarse-grained and enterprise-scoped; microservices are fine-grained, each bounded to a single business capability.
- **Communication** – SOA uses a smart central ESB with heavyweight protocols (SOAP); microservices use smart endpoints and dumb pipes (REST, gRPC, Kafka).
- **Data ownership** – SOA services often share a common database; microservices follow database-per-service.
- **Governance** – SOA has centralized governance with canonical data models; microservices embrace decentralized, polyglot governance.
- **Deployment** – SOA services deploy in larger units; microservices are independently deployable and independently scalable.
s1_definition.analogy: Think of National Bank of India. The SOA way is a few large departments that route every request through one central mailroom (the ESB) and all share one giant filing cabinet (shared database). The microservices way is many small specialized teams, each with its own filing cabinet, talking directly by simple notes (REST or messages), each renovating whenever it wants without asking central authority.

sections.s6_takeaway:
SOA and microservices are both ways to build a system as collaborating services, and microservices are really an evolution of SOA ideas made practical by containers and cloud. They differ on four dimensions. On granularity, SOA services are coarse-grained and enterprise-scoped while microservices are fine-grained and bounded to a single capability. On communication, SOA uses a smart central ESB while microservices use smart endpoints and dumb pipes. On data, SOA services often share a database while microservices follow database-per-service. On governance, SOA is centralized while microservices are decentralized and polyglot.

At National Bank of India, the ESB had become a bottleneck and single point of failure, so when it had problems the whole bank stalled. Moving to direct lightweight communication with database-per-service fixed that coupling, but added distributed complexity that only paid off because multiple teams genuinely needed independent deployment and scaling.

The most important thing is that neither is universally better. Microservices buy independence but cost distributed complexity, eventual consistency, and heavy operational overhead. For a small team or simple domain, a well-structured monolith may be the right choice, and recognizing that trade-off is the mark of seniority.

Remember one sentence: SOA uses coarse-grained services on a smart central ESB sharing data under centralized governance, while microservices use fine-grained, independently deployable services with smart endpoints, dumb pipes, and database-per-service under decentralized governance.
